brewing.notes: A safe starting point for dark tea: rinse once, boiling water, or simmer it the traditional way.

description:
A shrub tea variety native to Yuntai Mountain in Anhua County, Hunan, grown mainly around Anhua and Xinhua and a core raw material of Anhua dark tea.

Used above all as raw leaf for Anhua dark tea.
history: It was promoted across Hunan's tea districts from the 1950s into the later 1970s. A 1965 national conference on tea varieties in Fuzhou listed it among the first 21 notable population varieties and renamed it Yuntaishan Da Ye Cha, the name later used in university textbooks.
processing: A plant cultivar, not a processing style: it is usually made into dark tea, and the method is up to the grower.
harvest_season: Depends on the place and the grower.
appearance_dry: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
appearance_liquor: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
appearance_wet: Plump yellow-green shoots with moderate down; thick, soft long-elliptic leaves.
taste_profile: Dark tea made from it gives a clear, bright red liquor with a mellow, sweet, refreshing taste.
vintage_note: A cultivar is not sold by vintage. Tea made from it follows the usual pattern for dark tea, so ask for the harvest year and the grower.
